summary: Join our in-depth training on Basel III and discover the essential functions of central banks. Equip yourself with vital knowledge for the financial sector.
lede: Basel III training helps banking and financial-stability professionals interpret prudential requirements and understand central banks’ role in supervision. It covers assessing capital adequacy, buffers and leverage; interpreting liquidity standards for treasury and funding decisions; and using stress tests, supervisory review and clear reporting to support resilience. The course is relevant to bank risk, treasury, finance, compliance and audit teams, central bank supervision staff and board members.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals involved in various aspects of banking and financial stability. It targets those who need to understand and apply Basel III principles in their roles.
audience: Central bank supervision and regulation teams
Financial stability and macroprudential policy staff
Bank risk managers (credit, market, operational risk)
Internal auditors and risk assurance professionals
Board members, senior managers, and executives
modules: Basel III in Plain Language: What Problem Was It Built to Solve?
The Role of Central Banks in Financial Stability
Capital Adequacy: Understanding the Building Blocks
Capital Buffers: The Shock Absorbers Most Teams Misunderstand
Leverage Ratio: The Backstop Against “Too Clever” Balance Sheets
Liquidity Standards That Shape Daily Treasury Decisions
Stress Testing and Resilience: What Happens Under Shock?
Supervisory Review and ICAAP/ILAAP in Practical Terms
Macroprudential Policy: How Central Banks Manage System-Wide Risk
Basel III Trade-Offs: Growth, Profitability, and Stability
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of banking operations, risk management, and financial regulations. Prior experience in finance or related fields is recommended.
